India’s extreme poverty rate has fallen sharply, dropping from 27.1% in 2011 to 2.6% in 2023, according to the World Bank. Its estimates suggest around 496 million people moved above the lower-middle-income poverty line during this period.
But the numbers reveal another side of India’s economic story. The wage gap between the richest and poorest workers remains significant, poverty is concentrated in certain regions, and concerns persist over stagnant real earnings, job quality and youth unemployment.
